field:rack::engine::Cable::id.finding: P2: the setter refuses IDs below -1 and from 2**53 up (native/bindings/engine/cable.cpp:218). Rack does not need either limit: Engine::addCable_NoLock treats any negative ID as unset and accepts any free int64 ID. docs/reference/engine.md#engine-cables only says '-1 until the engine assigns one', so the limit is undocumented. Fix: accept any int64, or document the range with its reason in #engine-cables.

method:rack::engine::Engine::setMasterMo.finding: P1: the binding refuses a module that is not in the engine (native/bindings/engine/engine.cpp:321, through engineModule, engine_internal.hpp:108-111). Rack's Engine.hpp says 'Module does not need to belong to the Engine'. Fix: document the requirement and its reason in #engine-master.

method:rack::engine::Engine::setSuggeste.finding: P1: the binding raises ValueError for NaN, negative and infinite rates (native/bindings/engine/engine.cpp:357-358; tested at test_engine.py:61). Only infinity is a real hazard (sampleTime would be 0). Rack's Engine::setSuggestedSampleRate (src/engine/Engine.cpp:663-674) sends anything not > 0, NaN and negatives included, to the 44100 fallback, so refusing those is an unjustified restriction. docs/reference/engine.md#engine-master documents only '0 gives Rack's fallback'. Fix: refuse only +inf (or document the limits and their reason).

method:rack::engine::Engine::updateParam.finding: P0: crash on another owner's handle. For a handle with ours() false, the lambda runs inside locked() (engine_internal.hpp:99-105), which has already released the GIL. It then calls updatable() (native/bindings/engine/param_handle.cpp:331), which calls ref.get(false) (param_handle.cpp:191), which calls findForeign(false). That opens a second py::gil_scoped_release (param_handle.cpp:136) while the GIL is not held. pybind11 3.1 requires the GIL there and PyEval_SaveThread fails fatally; it also takes a second EngineLease shared lock on the same thread. Such handles are reachable: get_param_handle returns views of other owners' handles, and nothing refuses them here. docs/reference/engine.md#engine-param-handles calls those views 'read-only', yet the binding tries to update them. No test covers a foreign handle. Fix: refuse foreign handles in update_param_handle, as the docs imply, or resolve them inside the locked lambda with engine.getParamHandle(ref.moduleId, ref.paramId) and no nested release. Add a test with a foreign handle.
